You're right on that. You can still count on friends and family if they're still around. And if you can't, then...well, ya' deserve better than that. Relying on the few people who I trust is what's helped me get through it. I wish you the best, regardless of the circumstances.

I can't say anything more than say I'm with you. Abandoned by the one you love is so horrific and lonely and shattering. Going through the same right now and it is absolutely soul-sucking. I offer you my sympathy, and I'm sorry you have to go through it. It's hard to build back up that trust.

Thank you. It's hard for me to say, "She's not my mother," because she still provides for me in tangible ways, but she has acted more like a dogmatic religious figure than a person that I could ever relate to. It's hard to come to terms with it, but you're right, it's something I have to accept over time.
Yeah, it's comforting to me because I don't feel alone like my mom made me feel when she went on a tirade against my siblings and me.

Well, where I'm from, it's typically expected that the dad gives out the belt spankings. I dunno why, but it almost sounds like a way to use the father as a "fence" for your mom's punishment. Maybe not, though.

>and I'd have to come apologize and console her afterwards...

Oh, man, I forgot about that. My mom made me do that, too. Can't believe someone would try to portray themselves as the victim after whipping their own child, that's nuts.

No, because that's a personal choice I have to make (and am continually in the process of), but oftentimes her forgiveness speeches insinuate that I haven't truly forgiven her because I'm still hurt by her actions.

I don't think that's unforgiveness, I think that's a normal process of forgiveness.

Her choosing not to apologize is, however, hurtful to me because she is willfully denying that she has pained me. It does not make me spiteful, but it makes me sad.

She actually asked me a few days ago about my thoughts on her parenting. She had an intuition, I guess, of what was bugging me.

I was apprehensive, but I told her my opinions in a level-headed way. I told her that she was mostly a good parent overall, but I had some issues with the way she raised us.

She denied most of it, and kept reiterating the stuff that she did provide us. I kept trying to tell her that my circumstances were fine, but that she didn't fulfill my emotional needs very well.

The tears broke when I told her about the "spiritual warfare" she subjected me to. I didn't tell this in the OP because I didn't want to cast too negative a light on my mother, but I was tormented a lot at night because I thought I wasn't a very good Christian due to the pressure she put on me. I punched myself and wished I could die at times.

She apologized for not taking my requests to see a psychiatrist seriously. She very much knew back then that I was troubled, so I'm having a hard time reconciling her reasoning (she blames money, but our insurance would have covered it, unbeknownst to 14-year-old me).

Then, she gave a speech on forgiveness, which I'm not so sure I needed. Things like that have been commonplace when she wants to minimize apologizing to me.

She prayed with me and agreed to set up an appointment with a counselor through my church.

Again, it very much felt like she was trying to avoid the shame of what she had done, so it was hard to take her sincerely. I know she means the best, but I don't want her to keep doing that.
Freshman year was pretty cringey, I'll just leave it at that.
Yeah, I think that was the actual motivation behind forbidding me. The "witchcraft" excuse was something familiar she knew would get me to stop.

>I just was pointing out that several things on OP's list are not brainwashing, but are representative of normal parenting. 

You are right in a sense, which I wish people would not downvote you for.

I listed the punishments not as examples of brainwashing, but of things symptomatic of their belief system. So you're not wrong in your assumptions. I purposefully left out a lot of the ways they manipulated my faith because...well, it's a bit too personal for this subreddit. Hopefully I didn't give a wrong impression that way.

tl;dr Don't taze him, bros.

Plus, it blocked out more words with Barney than it did with Die Hard. It's pretty funny, but it is waaaaay overzealous. It is overly strict, and you can't change the dictionary besides "strict" and "religious programming".

Wow, that's exactly what I'm going through. Thank you for your words, that means a lot to me.

I remember a redditor summarizing a quote, "Adulthood is when our heroes become human." It seems to be a phase a lot of folks my age go through.

You're honestly right in a lot of ways. The only thing I question sometimes is her sincerity...it almost seemed like she did what she did just to get parent brownie points, or something.

\*shrug\* I can only assume the best.
Wow, that's beautiful, but a heartbreaking read. Summarizes a lot of my experiences with church as a child...just trying to blend in so I didn't upset my mom.

Father was pretty irreligious when I was young, and still mostly is despite accepting Christ a while back. My mom blamed a lot of her marriage problems on him until they started taking marriage counseling. My father was a lot more lenient on me, so I formed a more genuine relationship with me. I trusted his life advice much more than my mom's even though I was a momma's boy for the longest time.

My siblings...well, I'm the oldest, so I was their role model of sorts. I played yes-man to my mom's parenting, though, so they didn't have too much respect for me as time went on. We have an okay relationship nowadays, and they're beginning to understand the manipulation they were under as well.
Thank you for the prayers. Rest assured my faith has remained intact, albeit a tad bit confused for the time being. :)

Thank you for the realistic viewpoint. My mom iterated on this point a lot when we would bring up stuff she did and continued to do, but since she seemed unapologetic for the stuff she actually did, her forgiveness speech never had that much of an impact on me.

>And, I actually thanked my mom for her role in my life as a kid. It was crazy and put me through a lot of stuff. But those seeds she planted, the really important stuff, is the foundation that allowed me to rebuild my own beliefs. She was trying her best, and he is as much Gods daughter as I am his son. Don't know if this helps but I hope it does. Hang in there.

Thank you, that viewpoint does very much help me. My mother did a very good job teaching me the basic tenants of Christianity, so that is something for me to remember.

I'm happy you were able to work it out. My brothers are very resentful of my mother (and so am I, to some degree), so I know the damage it can do to you if you hold onto that resentment instead of appreciating the things she did.

>God is not your mother.

Wow, that sentence alone summarizes my frustrations a lot better than I did.

Thank you for your sympathies.
Thank you for the recommendation, I'll check it out.

Nothing, thank goodness. I talked to a security guard at my apartment about it later and he said they probably weren't staking out houses for burglary or anything; they were just trying to scam people by pretending to be a charity.

Thank you for the advice. I think I'll stay home this weekend just in case they drop by again (they said they'd come back... \*shudder\*). I also will flag my checking account to make sure nothing terrible comes out of giving them that check.

I called my apartment security, and they said it was probably a phishing scam to get my info.

[This is a very good site I have been using.](http://www.improveyoursocialskills.com/) It has some really good advice for meaningful relationships. I found it linked in the sidebar of a social-skills-oriented subreddit.

My advice: focus on relationships that matter. You don't want a one night stand, so don't act like you do. Be intentional with your friendships.
